subject: Portability check & migration tactics for hosting: hosted / dedicated / private
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Portability check & migration tactics for hosting: hosted / dedicated / private

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have aligned next steps: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary drivers: reduce token cost, improve tail latency, and prepare for a PHI-enabled workload later this year.
- Current environment: self-hosted LLM on-prem (you mentioned legacy GPU clusters) with an API shim today.
- Key constraints: data residency in US, SOC2 evidence request during procurement, and procurement timeline target: mid-July.

Open questions we flagged for qualification:
1) Do you expect to serve PHI within the first 6 months, or after an initial pilot? (affects Private/VPC timing)
2) Are you comfortable with a staged migration (start on Redwood Dedicated, then migrate to Private VPC), or do you require Private from day one?
3) Which parts of the workload require low single-digit tail latency vs which can tolerate batching for cost savings?
4) Current cluster specifics: GPU type, orchestration (Kubernetes, Slurm), and any on-prem network egress constraints.

Next steps we recommend:
- Technical deep-dive / migration workshop (90 minutes) with Laura (solutions) and Karthik (platform architect).
- Share your procurement timeline and preferred contract terms so we can align quotes for Dedicated vs Private.
- I attached a short hosting comparison and a draft SOW so you can see ballpark timelines/price bands.

Can you confirm availability for the workshop next week? Also please loop Sarah from procurement so we can start the procurement checklist.

Thanks —

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW-draft-archer-v1.pdf (stub), redwood-hosting-comparison.xlsx (stub)
From: Mike Allen <mike@archerhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@archerhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Portability check & migration tactics for hosting: hosted / dedicated / private

Thanks Olga —

Good summary. A few quick answers:
- PHI: We expect to start with non-PHI features for a Q3 pilot and then expand to PHI in Q4. So we want a solution that can transition to Private/VPC later, but we don't need Private day one.
- Staging: Prefer staged (Dedicated -> Private) if the migration path is straightforward.
- Latency: Core clinical search responses need <150ms p95; batch job features (analytics, offline reranking) can be slower.
- Cluster: On-prem cluster is A100-based, managed with internal Kubernetes (openshift). Network egress is proxied — we'll need to validate firewall rules.

Procurement: Sarah is copied — we have an internal procurement window that expects vendor selection by 2027-07-15. Can you provide an initial cost comparison and an outline of the onboarding timeline for Dedicated vs Private? Also we need a high-level list of SOC2 artifacts we would get during evaluation.

—Mike

Mike / Sarah —

Appreciate the fast responses. Based on the answers here is a proposed path that balances speed to pilot with a controlled move to Private for PHI later:

Option A — Dedicated-first (recommended for pilot):
- Timeline: 2–4 weeks to provision a Dedicated pool and 4–6 weeks to complete onboarding + integration tests.
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, predictable throughput, simpler procurement (reserved capacity).
- Cons: additional work later to migrate KV cache and fine-tune latency profiles when moving to Private.

Option B — Private VPC (if you must have Private day 1):
- Timeline: 8–12 weeks for VPC/private setup, networking, and KMS integration.
- Pros: full data isolation and easier PHI compliance once set up.
- Cons: longer lead time and larger initial contract.

Migration considerations we noted:
- We can support a staged migration: start on Dedicated and perform a controlled cutover to Private when you are ready. Our migration workshop will produce a mutual action plan with cutover steps, cache sync notes, and rollback triggers.
- For your on-prem Kubernetes + A100 cluster, we can provide an ingestion adaptor and a compatibility checklist so you can parallel-run requests if you prefer.

Next recommended actions:
1) Schedule a 90-minute migration workshop (Laura + Karthik + Rishi on our side). Proposed windows: Apr 19 (Tue) 10:00–11:30 PT or Apr 21 (Thu) 13:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm which works.
2) I attached a short SOC2 artifact list and an initial draft SOW for procurement.
3) If procurement prefers, we can provide a scoped SOW for a Dedicated pilot with an optional Private transition addendum.

I'll ask Rishi to draft a high-level pricing band for Dedicated vs Private and share a preliminary estimate by EOD Apr 14.

Thanks —

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
